value.rationale: The integer-radicand problem recently settled by Pisani has a genuine arithmetic sensitivity to rational scaling. The evaluated genus transition separates infinite low-degree families from finite higher-degree loci, and an explicit non-torsion elliptic point proves the k=4 boundary is attained. These are natural structural answers about that same simultaneous-rationality question, not arbitrary finite instances; a broad finiteness theorem alone does not provide the phase-sharp low-degree examples.
